short_description.id: Naga dari Utara atau Katak Utara (Põhja konn) adalah monster raksasa mirip katak dalam cerita rakyat Estonia yang memorakporandakan negeri sampai dikalahkan seorang pemuda dengan cincin ajaib.
short_description.en: The Dragon of the North or Northern Frog (Põhja konn) is a giant frog-like monster of Estonian lore that ravages the land until a young man defeats it with a magic ring.

long_description.id: Naga dari Utara, atau Katak Utara, adalah monster raksasa mirip katak dalam cerita rakyat Estonia. Ia datang dari Utara, menghancurkan wilayah-wilayah luas dan memangsa manusia serta hewan. Tubuhnya tertutup sisik yang lebih kuat dari batu dan besi, dan kedua mata besarnya bersinar siang dan malam seperti lilin.
long_description.en: The Dragon of the North, or Northern Frog, is a giant frog-like monster of Estonian lore. It came out of the North, laying waste whole tracts of country and devouring men and beasts. Its body was covered with scales stronger than stone and iron, and its two great eyes shone day and night like candles.

long_description.id: Kisahnya dipopulerkan Friedrich Reinhold Kreutzwald dalam kumpulan dongeng tahun 1866 dengan judul "Põhja Konn". Seorang pemuda memperoleh cincin meterai dan memakainya untuk mengalahkan binatang itu, setelah seorang raja menawarkan putri dan separuh kerajaannya kepada siapa pun yang bisa membunuhnya. Lewat terjemahan Jerman, kisah ini masuk ke The Yellow Fairy Book (1894) karya Andrew Lang dan Leonora Blanche Lang.
long_description.en: The tale was popularised by Friedrich Reinhold Kreutzwald in his 1866 collection under the title "Põhja Konn". A young man obtains a signet ring and uses it to defeat the beast, after a king offers his daughter and half his kingdom to whoever can kill it. Through a German translation the story entered The Yellow Fairy Book (1894) by Andrew Lang and Leonora Blanche Lang.

long_description.id: Risto Järv menggolongkan kisah ini sebagai varian lokal kisah pembunuh naga (ATU 300) dengan katak menggantikan naga, dan menurut August Annist, Kreutzwald sendiri yang membuat naganya mirip katak saat menyesuaikan kisah itu dengan konteks Estonia. Karya modern justru sering menjadikan katak itu pelindung, misalnya novel Andrus Kivirähk dan patung karya Navitrolla.
long_description.en: Risto Järv classes the tale as a local variant of the dragon-slayer story (ATU 300) with the frog replacing the dragon, and according to August Annist it was Kreutzwald who made the dragon frog-like when adapting the story to the Estonian setting. Modern works often recast the frog as a protector, as in Andrus Kivirähk's novel and Navitrolla's statue.

short_description.id: Eryr Gwern Abwy, Elang Gwern Abwy, adalah salah satu Hewan Tertua dalam mitologi Wales yang muncul dalam kisah Culhwch ac Olwen dan menuntun para utusan Arthur kepada Salmon dari Llyn Llyw.
short_description.en: The Eagle of Gwern Abwy (Eryr Gwern Abwy) is one of the Oldest Animals of the mythology of Wales who appears in the tale of Culhwch ac Olwen and guides Arthur's envoys to the Salmon of Llyn Llyw.

long_description.id: Eryr Gwern Abwy adalah salah satu Hewan Tertua (Anifeiliaid Hynaf) dalam mitologi Wales dan disebut dalam kisah Culhwch ac Olwen. Dalam Trioedd ia termasuk Tri Hynaif Byd bersama Tylluan Cwm Cowlyd dan Mwyalchen Gelli Gadarn. Lokasi Gwern Abwy sendiri tidak diketahui. Elang adalah burung penting dalam mitologi bangsa Kelt (Celtiaid) dan dikaitkan dengan Matahari.
long_description.en: Eryr Gwern Abwy is one of the Oldest Animals (Anifeiliaid Hynaf) in the mythology of Wales and is mentioned in the tale Culhwch ac Olwen. In the Trioedd he is among the Tri Hynaif Byd alongside Tylluan Cwm Cowlyd and Mwyalchen Gelli Gadarn. The location of Gwern Abwy itself is unknown. The eagle (eryr) is an important bird in the mythology of the Celtiaid and is associated with the Sun.

long_description.id: Dalam terjemahan kisah itu, burung hantu menuntun para utusan ke Elang Gwern Abwy, yang disebut sebagai makhluk paling tua sekaligus paling jauh mengembara. Elang itu bercerita tentang sebuah batu yang dahulu ia patuk bintang-bintangnya dari puncak dan kini tingginya tak sampai sejengkal. Para utusan menanyakan Mabon, putra Modron.
long_description.en: In the translation of the tale, the owl leads the envoys to the Eagle of Gwern Abwy, described as the most ancient creature and the greatest traveller. The eagle speaks of a rock from whose summit he once pecked at the stars, now no more than a span tall. The envoys ask after Mabon the son of Modron.

long_description.id: Elang itu tidak tahu di mana Mabon berada, kecuali sekali ketika ia mencari makan sampai ke Llyn Llyw dan mencengkeram seekor salmon yang menyeretnya ke kedalaman. Ia lalu menuntun para utusan kepada salmon itu, Eog Llyn Llyw, yang diduga tahu lebih banyak.
long_description.en: The eagle does not know where Mabon is, except that once, searching for food as far as Llyn Llyw, he struck a salmon that dragged him into the deep. He then guides the envoys to that salmon, Eog Llyn Llyw, who may know more.

short_description.id: Eryr Gwern Abwy, Elang Gwern Abwy, adalah salah satu Hewan Tertua dalam mitologi Wales yang muncul dalam kisah Culhwch ac Olwen dan menuntun para utusan Arthur kepada Salmon dari Llyn Llyw.
short_description.en: The Eagle of Gwern Abwy (Eryr Gwern Abwy) is one of the Oldest Animals of the mythology of Wales who appears in the tale of Culhwch ac Olwen and guides Arthur's envoys to the Salmon of Llyn Llyw.

long_description.id: Eryr Gwern Abwy adalah salah satu Hewan Tertua (Anifeiliaid Hynaf) dalam mitologi Wales dan disebut dalam kisah Culhwch ac Olwen. Dalam Trioedd ia termasuk Tri Hynaif Byd bersama Tylluan Cwm Cowlyd dan Mwyalchen Gelli Gadarn. Lokasi Gwern Abwy sendiri tidak diketahui. Elang adalah burung penting dalam mitologi bangsa Kelt (Celtiaid) dan dikaitkan dengan Matahari.
long_description.en: Eryr Gwern Abwy is one of the Oldest Animals (Anifeiliaid Hynaf) in the mythology of Wales and is mentioned in the tale Culhwch ac Olwen. In the Trioedd he is among the Tri Hynaif Byd alongside Tylluan Cwm Cowlyd and Mwyalchen Gelli Gadarn. The location of Gwern Abwy itself is unknown. The eagle (eryr) is an important bird in the mythology of the Celtiaid and is associated with the Sun.

long_description.id: Dalam terjemahan kisah itu, burung hantu menuntun para utusan ke Elang Gwern Abwy, yang disebut sebagai makhluk paling tua sekaligus paling jauh mengembara. Elang itu bercerita tentang sebuah batu yang dahulu ia patuk bintang-bintangnya dari puncak dan kini tingginya tak sampai sejengkal. Para utusan menanyakan Mabon, putra Modron.
long_description.en: In the translation of the tale, the owl leads the envoys to the Eagle of Gwern Abwy, described as the most ancient creature and the greatest traveller. The eagle speaks of a rock from whose summit he once pecked at the stars, now no more than a span tall. The envoys ask after Mabon the son of Modron.

long_description.id: Elang itu tidak tahu di mana Mabon berada, kecuali sekali ketika ia mencari makan sampai ke Llyn Llyw dan mencengkeram seekor salmon yang menyeretnya ke kedalaman. Ia lalu menuntun para utusan kepada salmon itu, Eog Llyn Llyw, yang diduga tahu lebih banyak.
long_description.en: The eagle does not know where Mabon is, except that once, searching for food as far as Llyn Llyw, he struck a salmon that dragged him into the deep. He then guides the envoys to that salmon, Eog Llyn Llyw, who may know more.

short_description.id: Loong adalah naga dalam mitologi Tiongkok, lazim digambarkan menyerupai ular dengan empat kaki.
short_description.en: Loong belongs to Chinese mythology and commonly has a serpentine shape with four legs.

long_description.id: Loong adalah naga dalam mitologi Tiongkok, lazim digambarkan menyerupai ular dengan empat kaki. Naga menjadi lambang kekuasaan kaisar dalam sejarah Tiongkok.
long_description.en: Loong belongs to Chinese mythology and commonly has a serpentine shape with four legs. The dragon served as an emblem of imperial authority in Chinese history.

long_description.id: Bentuk naga melingkar juga ditemukan pada amulet giok zaman Shang. Sebagian benda yang dahulu disebut tulang naga ternyata fosil mamalia. Wang Fu mencatat tradisi sembilan kemiripan anatomi naga dengan hewan lain. Doré mencatat varian anatomi dengan tanduk rusa dan kepala buaya. Naga dalam seni sering mengejar atau memperebutkan mutiara menyala. Kepercayaan populer menghubungkan naga dengan sungai, laut, dan pengaturan hujan. Saat kekeringan atau banjir, masyarakat melakukan ritual untuk memohon bantuan raja naga setempat. Sebuah legenda mengisahkan Kaisar Kuning naik ke langit setelah menjadi naga. Museum Norton menjelaskan naga sebagai penguasa langit yang dimohon mendatangkan hujan dalam ritual. Pada jubah istana, naga merujuk pada mandat kaisar untuk memerintah dari Takhta Naga. Museum V&A menafsirkan mutiara menyala dalam motif naga sebagai kebijaksanaan, pencerahan, dan hakikat spiritual. Pola naga pada keramik ekspor Tiongkok mengilhami keramik cetak biru-putih Inggris abad kesembilan belas. V&A mencatat bahwa pola piring Inggris mengikuti porselen biru-putih yang diekspor dari Tiongkok pada abad ketujuh belas dan kedelapan belas.
long_description.en: Coiled dragon forms occur on jade amulets from the Shang period. Scientific examination identifies many objects called dragon bones as mammal fossils. Wang Fu recorded a tradition of nine animal resemblances in dragon anatomy. Doré records an anatomical variant with deer antlers and a crocodile head. Art often shows dragons pursuing or contesting a flaming pearl. Popular belief connects dragons with rivers, seas, and the distribution of rain. During drought or flooding, villagers offered sacrifices and religious rites to appease local dragon kings and seek rain. One legend describes the Yellow Emperor ascending to heaven after becoming a dragon. The Norton Museum describes dragons as heavenly rulers petitioned for rain through ritual. On court robes, dragon imagery refers to the emperor’s mandate to rule from the Dragon Throne. The V&A interprets the flaming pearl in dragon imagery as wisdom, enlightenment, and spiritual essence. Dragon patterns on Chinese export ceramics inspired British printed blue-and-white wares in the nineteenth century. The V&A notes that the British plate pattern follows blue-and-white porcelain exported from China in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

claims.quote: The Chinese dragon, known as long or loong (/lʊŋ/ LUUNG) is a legendary creature in Chinese mythology, Chinese folklore, and Chinese culture generally. Chinese dragons have many animal-like forms, such as turtles and fish, but are most commonly depicted as snake-like with four legs.

statement.id: Loong adalah naga dalam mitologi Tiongkok, lazim digambarkan menyerupai ular dengan empat kaki.
statement.en: Loong belongs to Chinese mythology and commonly has a serpentine shape with four legs.

claims.quote: Historically, the Chinese dragon was associated with the emperor of China and used as a symbol to represent imperial power. Liu Bang, the founder of the Han dynasty, claimed that he was conceived after his mother dreamt of a dragon. During the Tang dynasty, emperors wore robes with dragon motif as an imperial symbol, and high officials might also be presented with dragon robes.

statement.id: Naga menjadi lambang kekuasaan kaisar dalam sejarah Tiongkok.
statement.en: The dragon served as an emblem of imperial authority in Chinese history.

claims.quote: The coiled dragon or snake form played an important role in early Chinese culture. The character for "dragon" in the earliest Chinese writing has a similar coiled form, as do later jade dragon amulets from the Shang period.

statement.id: Bentuk naga melingkar juga ditemukan pada amulet giok zaman Shang.
statement.en: Coiled dragon forms occur on jade amulets from the Shang period.

claims.quote: Scientific examination of "dragon bones" from the 19th century to the present suggests they most commonly are remains of fossil Cenozoic mammals, such as the extinct horse Hipparion.

statement.id: Sebagian benda yang dahulu disebut tulang naga ternyata fosil mamalia.
statement.en: Scientific examination identifies many objects called dragon bones as mammal fossils.

claims.quote: From its origins as totems or the stylized depiction of natural creatures, the Chinese dragon evolved to become a mythical animal. The Han dynasty scholar Wang Fu recorded Chinese myths that long dragons had nine anatomical resemblances.

statement.id: Wang Fu mencatat tradisi sembilan kemiripan anatomi naga dengan hewan lain.
statement.en: Wang Fu recorded a tradition of nine animal resemblances in dragon anatomy.

claims.quote: "The antlers of a deer. The head of a crocodile. A demon's eyes. The neck of a snake. A tortoise's viscera. A hawk's claws. The palms of a tiger. A cow's ears. And it hears through its horns, its ears being deprived of all power of hearing".

statement.id: Doré mencatat varian anatomi dengan tanduk rusa dan kepala buaya.
statement.en: Doré records an anatomical variant with deer antlers and a crocodile head.

claims.quote: Many pictures of Chinese dragons show a flaming pearl under their chin or in their claws. The pearl is associated with spiritual energy, wisdom, prosperity, power, immortality, thunder, or the moon. Chinese art often depicts a pair of dragons chasing or fighting over a flaming pearl.

statement.en: Art often shows dragons pursuing or contesting a flaming pearl.

claims.quote: Chinese dragons are strongly associated with water and weather in popular religion. They are believed to be the rulers of moving bodies of water, such as waterfalls, rivers, or seas. The Dragon god is the dispenser of rain as well as the zoomorphic representation of yang, the masculine power of generation.

claims.quote: Because of this association, they are seen as "in charge" of water-related weather phenomena. In premodern times, many Chinese villages (especially those close to rivers and seas) had temples dedicated to their local "dragon king".

short_description.id: Markut, juga disebut Merküt atau Bürküt, adalah burung legendaris berwujud elang dalam tradisi Altai dan Mongol yang melindungi dan membimbing dukun; di kalangan Yörük di Anatolia ia menjadi sosok untuk menakuti anak nakal.
short_description.en: Markut, also called Merküt or Bürküt, is a legendary eagle-like bird of Altay and Mongol tradition that protects and guides shamans; among the Yörüks of Anatolia it became a figure used to frighten naughty children.

long_description.id: Menurut kamus kedua, Markut adalah elang legendaris dalam mitologi Altai dan Mongol. Ia menjaga para dukun, menuntun jiwa mereka saat melakukan perjalanan ke langit, dan menggendong mereka kembali ke bumi bila tenaga mereka habis. Dalam doa dukun Altai, ia disapa sebagai burung yang sayap kirinya menutupi Bulan, sayap kanannya Matahari, dan sebagai ibu sembilan elang.
long_description.en: According to the second source, Markut is a legendary eagle in Altay and Mongol mythology. It watches over shamans, leads their souls on the journey into the sky and carries them back down to earth on its back once their strength fails. Altai shamans' prayers address it as the bird whose left wing hides the Moon and whose right wing hides the Sun, and as the mother of nine eagles.

long_description.id: Artikel pertama mengutip catatan Radlov tentang ritual kurban dukun di Pegunungan Altai. Markut di sana tidak kasatmata, hanya bisa dilihat orang tertentu, dan dipanggil untuk mengusir roh jahat. Setelah burung itu menjawab panggilan, dukun menirukan suaranya lalu menekuk leher untuk memperlihatkan beratnya memikul burung besar itu.
long_description.en: The first article draws on Radlov's account of shamans' sacrificial rites in the Altay mountains. There Markut is unseen, visible only to certain people, and is called upon to scare off evil spirits. Once the bird answers the call, the shaman imitates its cry and then bends his neck to show how heavy the great bird is to bear.

long_description.id: Pada genderang dukun Teleüt terdapat gambar burung berwujud elang besar bernama Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt, dan dalam pandangan dukun Altay-Sayan burung berwajah cahaya yang menemani Ülgen saat ritual juga disebut Merküt. Artikel pertama juga melihat kedekatan makna antara Markut, Bürküt Ata pada orang Turkmen, dan kepercayaan Yakut bahwa dukun berasal dari keturunan Bürküt.
long_description.en: Teleüt shamans' drums bear the image of a great eagle-like bird called Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt, and in the Altay-Sayan shamans' view the light-faced bird that accompanies Ülgen during rites is likewise called Merküt. The first article also notes a closeness in meaning between Markut, Bürküt Ata of the Turkmens and the Yakut belief that shamans descend from the Bürküt line.

long_description.id: Jauh dari Siberia, di kalangan Yörük semi-nomaden di Anatolia, Merküt menjadi makhluk khayalan yang dikaitkan dengan anak-anak. Di sana ia dikenal sebagai burung legendaris yang dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak nakal, dan menurut kepercayaan lama ia hanya menakuti orang yang namanya disebut.
long_description.en: Far from Siberia, among the semi-nomadic Yörüks of Anatolia, Merküt became an imaginary being connected with children. There it is known as a legendary bird used to scare naughty children, and in the old belief it frightens only those whose names are spoken.

statement.id: Markut, Merküt, atau Bürküt adalah burung legendaris (efsanevi kuş) di kalangan Yörük (Yörükler) yang direka untuk menakuti anak nakal; menurut kepercayaan lama, ia hanya menakuti orang yang namanya disebut.
statement.en: Markut, Merküt or Bürküt is a legendary bird (efsanevi kuş) among the Yörüks (Yörükler), invented to frighten naughty children; according to the old belief it only frightens those whose names are mentioned.

claims.quote: Kötü ruhları korkutmak amacıyla çağırılan Markut adındaki bu kuş ile Türkmenlerdeki Bürküt Ata ve Yakutların, şamanların Bürküt soyundan gelme inançları arasında mitolojik anlamsallık açısından yakınlık bulunmaktadır.

statement.id: Burung Markut yang dipanggil untuk menakuti roh jahat (kötü ruhları) memiliki kedekatan makna mitologis dengan Bürküt Ata pada orang Turkmen (Türkmenlerdeki) dan dengan kepercayaan Yakut (Yakutların) bahwa para dukun (şamanların) berasal dari keturunan Bürküt.
statement.en: The bird Markut, summoned to frighten evil spirits (kötü ruhları), is mythologically close to Bürküt Ata among the Turkmens (Türkmenlerdeki) and to the Yakut (Yakutların) belief that shamans (şamanların) descend from the Bürküt lineage.

claims.quote: Radlov'un sözünü ettiği Markut, göze görünmez ve kötü ruhları korkutmak için çağırılır. Bu kuşu ancak belli insanlar tarafından görüşebilir.

statement.id: Markut yang disebut Radlov tidak terlihat mata (göze görünmez) dan dipanggil untuk menakuti roh jahat; hanya orang tertentu (belli insanlar) yang dapat melihatnya.
statement.en: The Markut mentioned by Radlov is invisible (göze görünmez) and is summoned to frighten evil spirits; only certain people (belli insanlar) can see it.

claims.quote: Şaman, Markut kuşunu bu yolla çağırdıktan sonra cevap verdiği zaman, kuşun sesini taklit eder

statement.en: After the shaman (şaman) summons the Markut bird in this way and it answers, he imitates the bird's voice (kuşun sesini taklit eder).

claims.quote: Sonra büyük kuşun taşımasının ne kadar zor olduğunu göstermek için boynunu büker.

statement.en: One of the images on the drums of Teleüt shamans (Teleüt şamanlarının davullarında) is a bird called Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt, shaped like a great eagle.

claims.quote: Böylece Altay-Sayan şamanlarının dünya görüşünde kamlık zamanı ulu Ülgen'e yoldaşlık yapan nur yüzlü kuşun adı da "Merküt" olmuştur.

statement.id: Dalam pandangan dunia dukun Altay-Sayan, burung berwajah cahaya (nur yüzlü kuş) yang menemani Ülgen saat ritual dukun (kamlık) juga bernama Merküt.
statement.en: In the worldview of the Altay-Sayan shamans, the light-faced bird (nur yüzlü kuş) accompanying Ülgen during the shamanic rite (kamlık) is also named Merküt.

statement.en: This Merküt bird, far from Siberia (Sibirya), took the form among the semi-nomadic Yörüks of Anatolia (Anadolu) of an imaginary being that protects children (çocukları koruyan).

claims.quote: Altay ve Moğol mitolojisindeki efsânevî kartaldır. Şamanları korur ve göğe yaptıkları yolculukta yardımcı olarak ruhlarına kılavuzluk eder.

statement.id: Markut adalah elang legendaris (efsânevî kartal) dalam mitologi Altai (Altay) dan Mongol (Moğol); ia melindungi para dukun (şamanları korur) dan membimbing jiwa mereka dalam perjalanan ke langit (göğe yaptıkları yolculukta).

claims.quote: Güçleri tükenince sırtında yeryüzüne indirir. Anadolu'da yörük boyları arasında da rastlanan bir motiftir.

statement.en: When their strength runs out (güçleri tükenince), it carries them down to earth on its back; the motif is also found among the Yörük tribes of Anatolia (Anadolu'da yörük boyları).

short_description.id: Markut, juga disebut Merküt atau Bürküt, adalah burung legendaris berwujud elang dalam tradisi Altai dan Mongol yang melindungi dan membimbing dukun; di kalangan Yörük di Anatolia ia menjadi sosok untuk menakuti anak nakal.
short_description.en: Markut, also called Merküt or Bürküt, is a legendary eagle-like bird of Altay and Mongol tradition that protects and guides shamans; among the Yörüks of Anatolia it became a figure used to frighten naughty children.

long_description.id: Menurut kamus kedua, Markut adalah elang legendaris dalam mitologi Altai dan Mongol. Ia menjaga para dukun, menuntun jiwa mereka saat melakukan perjalanan ke langit, dan menggendong mereka kembali ke bumi bila tenaga mereka habis. Dalam doa dukun Altai, ia disapa sebagai burung yang sayap kirinya menutupi Bulan, sayap kanannya Matahari, dan sebagai ibu sembilan elang.
long_description.en: According to the second source, Markut is a legendary eagle in Altay and Mongol mythology. It watches over shamans, leads their souls on the journey into the sky and carries them back down to earth on its back once their strength fails. Altai shamans' prayers address it as the bird whose left wing hides the Moon and whose right wing hides the Sun, and as the mother of nine eagles.

long_description.id: Artikel pertama mengutip catatan Radlov tentang ritual kurban dukun di Pegunungan Altai. Markut di sana tidak kasatmata, hanya bisa dilihat orang tertentu, dan dipanggil untuk mengusir roh jahat. Setelah burung itu menjawab panggilan, dukun menirukan suaranya lalu menekuk leher untuk memperlihatkan beratnya memikul burung besar itu.
long_description.en: The first article draws on Radlov's account of shamans' sacrificial rites in the Altay mountains. There Markut is unseen, visible only to certain people, and is called upon to scare off evil spirits. Once the bird answers the call, the shaman imitates its cry and then bends his neck to show how heavy the great bird is to bear.

long_description.id: Pada genderang dukun Teleüt terdapat gambar burung berwujud elang besar bernama Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt, dan dalam pandangan dukun Altay-Sayan burung berwajah cahaya yang menemani Ülgen saat ritual juga disebut Merküt. Artikel pertama juga melihat kedekatan makna antara Markut, Bürküt Ata pada orang Turkmen, dan kepercayaan Yakut bahwa dukun berasal dari keturunan Bürküt.
long_description.en: Teleüt shamans' drums bear the image of a great eagle-like bird called Ülgen kuşu Bay Mörküt, and in the Altay-Sayan shamans' view the light-faced bird that accompanies Ülgen during rites is likewise called Merküt. The first article also notes a closeness in meaning between Markut, Bürküt Ata of the Turkmens and the Yakut belief that shamans descend from the Bürküt line.

long_description.id: Jauh dari Siberia, di kalangan Yörük semi-nomaden di Anatolia, Merküt menjadi makhluk khayalan yang dikaitkan dengan anak-anak. Di sana ia dikenal sebagai burung legendaris yang dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak nakal, dan menurut kepercayaan lama ia hanya menakuti orang yang namanya disebut.
long_description.en: Far from Siberia, among the semi-nomadic Yörüks of Anatolia, Merküt became an imaginary being connected with children. There it is known as a legendary bird used to scare naughty children, and in the old belief it frightens only those whose names are spoken.

short_description.id: Elang tanpa nama di puncak Yggdrasil adalah burung dalam mitologi Nordik yang bertengger di puncak pohon dunia, dengan elang kecil Veðrfölnir di antara kedua matanya, dan berselisih dengan naga Nidhöggr di akar pohon.
short_description.en: The unnamed eagle on the top of Yggdrasil is a bird of Norse mythology perched atop the world tree, with the hawk Veðrfölnir between its eyes, and at odds with the dragon Nidhöggr at the tree's roots.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, seekor elang yang namanya tidak diketahui bertengger di puncak pohon dunia Yggdrasil, dan di antara kedua matanya duduk elang kecil Veðrfölnir. Elang ini tercatat dalam Edda Puitis, yang dihimpun pada abad ke-13 dari bahan tradisional yang lebih tua, dan dalam Edda Prosa karya Snorri Sturluson, sedangkan Veðrfölnir hanya disebut dalam Edda Prosa.
long_description.en: In Norse mythology an eagle whose name is unknown perches at the top of the world tree Yggdrasil, and between its eyes sits the hawk Veðrfölnir. The eagle is attested in the Poetic Edda, compiled in the 13th century from older traditional material, and in Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda, whereas Veðrfölnir appears only in the Prose Edda.

long_description.id: Dalam Grímnismál, tupai Ratatoskr berlari di pohon ash Yggdrasil membawa kata-kata elang itu dari atas dan menyampaikannya kepada Nidhöggr di bawah. Dalam Gylfaginning dijelaskan bahwa seekor elang duduk di puncak pohon ash dan "mengetahui banyak hal", sementara Ratatoskr membawa gunjingan fitnah yang memancing permusuhan elang dan Nidhöggr. Bait Völuspá tentang "elang yang memekik" pada awal Ragnarök mungkin juga merujuk elang ini.
long_description.en: In Grímnismál the squirrel Ratatoskr runs on the ash Yggdrasil carrying the eagle's words from above and telling them to Nidhöggr below. Gylfaginning explains that an eagle sits at the top of the ash and 'has knowledge of many things', while Ratatoskr carries slanderous gossip that stirs up the eagle and Nidhöggr. The Völuspá verse about a 'screeching eagle' at the onset of Ragnarök may also refer to this eagle.

long_description.id: John Lindow mencatat bahwa Snorri tidak menjelaskan mengapa elang kecil duduk di antara mata elang atau apa perannya; menurutnya elang kecil itu barangkali terkait dengan kebijaksanaan elang, dan mungkin, seperti burung gagak Odin, terbang mengumpulkan dan membawa pulang pengetahuan.
long_description.en: John Lindow notes that Snorri does not say why a hawk should sit between the eagle's eyes or what role it plays; he suggests the hawk is presumably tied to the eagle's wisdom and perhaps, like Odin's ravens, flies off to gather and bring back knowledge.

statement.en: In Norse mythology Veðrfölnir is a hawk sitting between the eyes of an unnamed eagle perched on top of the world tree Yggdrasil.

claims.quote: The unnamed eagle is attested in both the Poetic Edda, compiled in the 13th century from earlier traditional sources, and the Prose Edda, written in the 13th century by Snorri Sturluson, while Veðrfölnir is solely attested in the Prose Edda.

claims.quote: There is much to be told. An eagle sits at the top of the ash, and it has knowledge of many things. Between its eyes sits the hawk called Vedrfolnir [...]. The squirrel called Ratatosk runs up and down the ash. He tells slanderous gossip, provoking the eagle and Nidhogg.

claims.quote: Das Gegensatzpaar Adler–Nidhöggr deutet darauf hin, dass auch diese Stelle des Lieds Völuspá den Weltenbaum-Adler meint, da man davon ausgeht, dass mit dem Nasenbleichen wohl Nidhöggr gemeint ist. Die Textstelle handelt vom Beginn der Ragnarök, der Endzeit der Götter.

statement.en: The eagle–Nidhöggr pairing suggests this Völuspá passage ('the eagle screams') also means the world-tree eagle, since the 'pale-nosed one' is taken to be Nidhöggr; the passage concerns the onset of Ragnarök.

claims.quote: John Lindow points out that Snorri does not say why a hawk should be sitting between the eyes of an eagle or what role it may play. short_description.id: Akbuzat adalah kuda putih bersayap mitologi Turkik, leluhur totem bangsa Bashkir dan Tatar dan kuda pahlawan Ural-Batyr, yang tinggal di langit dan ditambatkan pada Bintang Utara.
short_description.en: Akbuzat is the white winged horse of Turkic mythology, totem ancestor of the Bashkir and Tatar peoples and Ural-Batyr's heroic steed, who lives in the sky tethered to the Pole Star.

long_description.id: Akbuzat, "kuda bersayap yang terang", adalah kuda pahlawan dan leluhur totem bangsa-bangsa Turkik, lahir dari totemisme dan pemujaan kuda; warna putihnya melambangkan kehidupan dan kematian yang baik. Dalam mitologi Tatar, Akbuzat dan Kukbuzat tinggal di langit, turun membantu para pahlawan, lalu ditambatkan pada Bintang Utara sementara tujuh pencuri kuda, rasi Biduk, mengejar mereka tanpa hasil.
long_description.en: Akbuzat, 'light winged horse', is a heroic horse and totem ancestor of the Turkic peoples, born of totemism and the horse cult; its whiteness stands for a good life and death. In Tatar mythology Akbuzat and Kukbuzat live in the sky, come down to help heroes and are tethered to the Pole Star, while seven horse thieves, the Great Bear, chase them in vain.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Bashkir ia leluhur para tulpar dan kuda Ural-Batyr dalam epos Akbuzat; ia tidak terbakar atau tenggelam, menghancurkan gunung dengan kukunya, dan busa mulutnya menyembuhkan luka. Opera Akbuzat dipentaskan pada 1942, dan monumennya berdiri di Burzyansky sejak 2021.
long_description.en: In Bashkir mythology it is ancestor of the tulpars and Ural-Batyr's horse in the epic Akbuzat; it neither burns nor drowns, smashes mountains with its hooves, and its mouth foam heals wounds. The opera Akbuzat was staged in 1942, and its monument has stood in Burzyansky since 2021.

statement.en: Akbuzat's origin is tied to widespread totemism among Turkic peoples and the cult of the horse, while white symbolises a safe birth, a happy life, a peaceful death and a worthy burial.

statement.en: Tatar mythology tells of two divine heroic horses, Akbuzat and Kukbuzat (the sky-blue horse), who live in the sky, come down to help heroes, then return to the sky, tied to an iron stake.

short_description.id: Badraç adalah naga berkepala tujuh dalam mitologi Turk yang menyemburkan api, bersisik seperti zirah, dan hanya mati bila ketujuh kepalanya dipenggal.
short_description.en: Badraç is the seven-headed dragon of Turkic mythology: fire-breathing, armoured in scales, and killed only when all seven of its heads are cut off.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Turk, Badraç atau Padraç adalah naga berkepala tujuh. Ia menyemburkan api dari mulutnya, ekornya melecut seperti cambuk, dan kulitnya dilapisi sisik sekuat baju zirah. Karakurt mencatat bentuk nama lain seperti Badraş, Batraç, dan Padraş.
long_description.en: In Turkic mythology Badraç or Padraç is a seven-headed dragon. It spews fire from its mouth, its tail cracks like a whip, and its hide is covered in scales as strong as armour. Karakurt records other forms of the name such as Badraş, Batraç and Padraş.

long_description.id: Untuk membunuhnya, ketujuh kepalanya harus dipenggal; kalau tidak, kepala yang terpotong tumbuh lagi. Menurut sebagian legenda, kepala yang dipenggal satu per satu kembali ke tempatnya, sehingga ketujuhnya harus dipotong bersamaan. Karakurt menafsirkan banyaknya kepala sebagai lambang memiliki lebih dari satu nyawa.
long_description.en: To kill it, all seven heads must be cut off; otherwise a severed head grows back. In some legends heads cut off one at a time return to their place, so all seven must be cut at once. Karakurt interprets the many heads as a sign of having more than one life.

long_description.id: Salah satu sumber menyoroti bahwa gagasan naga muncul dengan berbagai nama di hampir setiap masyarakat. Sebagian orang bahkan menunjuk kalender Turk 12 hewan, yang menamai satu tahun dengan naga, sebagai petunjuk bahwa manusia pernah menyaksikan makhluk semacam itu.
long_description.en: One source notes that the dragon idea appears under various names in almost every society. Some even point to the 12-animal Turkic calendar, which names a year after the dragon, as a hint that humans once witnessed such a creature.

short_description.id: Ular Berbulu adalah dewa atau sosok supernatural penting dalam banyak agama Mesoamerika, dikenal sebagai Quetzalcōātl oleh orang Aztek dan Kukulkan oleh Maya Yukatek.
short_description.en: The Feathered Serpent is a prominent deity or supernatural entity of many Mesoamerican religions, known as Quetzalcōātl to the Aztecs and Kukulkan to the Yucatec Maya.

long_description.id: Ular Berbulu adalah sosok ilahi yang dipuja dalam banyak agama Mesoamerika. Orang Aztek menyebutnya Quetzalcōātl, Maya Yukatek menyebutnya Kukulkan, dan Maya Kʼicheʼ mengenalnya sebagai Qʼuqʼumatz dan Tohil. Bulunya ditafsirkan sebagai lambang sifat ilahi dan kemampuan terbang, sedangkan tubuh ularnya sebagai lambang sifat manusiawi yang melata di bumi.
long_description.en: The Feathered Serpent is a divine figure revered in many Mesoamerican religions. The Aztecs called it Quetzalcōātl, the Yucatec Maya Kukulkan, and the Kʼicheʼ Maya knew it as Qʼuqʼumatz and Tohil. Its feathers are read as a sign of divine nature and flight, its serpent body as a sign of a human nature that creeps on the earth.

long_description.id: Gambar ular berbulu sudah muncul dalam kebudayaan Olmek (sekitar 1400–400 SM), biasanya berupa ular derik berjambul. Di Teotihuacan (200 SM – 700 M) sosok ini menonjol di Kuil Ular Berbulu, dan secara umum paling sering tampil dalam arsitektur Mesoamerika.
long_description.en: Images of feathered serpents already appear in Olmec culture (c. 1400–400 BC), usually as a crested rattlesnake. At Teotihuacan (200 BC – 700 AD) the figure is prominent on the Temple of the Feathered Serpent, and overall it appears most often in Mesoamerican architecture.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, Ular Berbulu menguasai bintang pagi, menciptakan buku dan kalender, serta memberi jagung kepada manusia. Ia juga melambangkan kematian dan kelahiran kembali, dan menjadi pelindung para pendeta.
long_description.en: According to legend, the Feathered Serpent rules the morning star, invented books and the calendar, and gave maize to humanity. It also stands for death and rebirth and is the patron of priests.

short_description.id: Leucrota (leucrocuta) adalah hewan dongeng (fabeldier) keturunan crocotta yang dapat meniru suara manusia dan bergigi tulang utuh.
short_description.en: The leucrota (leucrocuta) is a fabulous beast (fabeldier) descended from the crocotta that can imitate human voices and has solid bone in place of teeth.

long_description.id: Leucrota (leucrocuta) adalah hewan dongeng (fabeldier), keturunan crocotta dengan hewan lain. Seperti crocotta yang mirip anjing, ia dapat meniru suara manusia, tetapi tubuhnya mirip antilop dengan kuku belah dan sangat cepat. Ia berpaha babi hutan (zwijn), berekor, berdada, dan berleher singa, serta berkepala luak; sebagai ganti gigi ia memiliki sisir tulang yang menghancurkan segalanya. Leucrota tidak pernah menutup mata, dan tulang punggungnya begitu kaku sehingga ia harus berbalik badan untuk melihat ke belakang.
long_description.en: The leucrota (leucrocuta) is a fabulous beast (fabeldier), the offspring of the crocotta and another animal. Like the dog-like crocotta it can imitate a human voice, but it resembles an antelope with cloven hooves and great speed. It has the thighs of a boar (zwijn), the tail, breast and neck of a lion and the head of a badger; instead of teeth it has bony ridges that grind everything. The leucrota never closes its eyes, and its spine is so stiff that it must turn round to see what is behind it.

long_description.id: Plinius menulis tentang leucrocotta, makhluk mirip hiena yang disebutnya hewan tercepat, sebesar keledai, berpaha rusa, berleher, berekor, dan berdada singa, berkepala luak, berkuku belah, bermulut terbuka sampai telinga, dan bertulang sebagai ganti gigi, yang konon meniru suara manusia. Bestiari dari masa kemudian mencampuradukkan berbagai kisah ini; Aberdeen Bestiary menyebut Leucrota hewan cepat yang lahir di India.
long_description.en: Pliny wrote of the leucrocotta, a hyena-like creature he called the fastest of all beasts: as big as an ass, with haunches like a stag, neck, tail and breast like a lion, a badger's head, split hooves, a mouth gaping back to the ears and ridges of bone where teeth should be, and reputed to mimic human voices. Later bestiaries of the Middle Ages muddled these accounts; the Aberdeen Bestiary calls the Leucrota a swift animal born in India.

short_description.id: Naga Rhodes adalah naga legenda yang meneror pulau Rhodes pada 1340-an sampai dibunuh ksatria Hospitaller Dieudonné de Gozon.
short_description.en: The dragon of Rhodes is a legendary dragon that terrorised Rhodes in the 1340s until killed by the Hospitaller knight Dieudonné de Gozon.

long_description.id: Naga Rhodes menurut legenda meneror lembah Soudourli di kaki gunung Santo Stefanus pada 1340-an, masa kekuasaan Ordo Hospitaller. Korbannya begitu banyak sehingga Grand Master Hélion de Villeneuve melarang para ksatria melawannya. Menurut Bosio naga itu sebesar kuda, berkepala ular, bertelinga bagal bersisik, dan bergigi tajam.
long_description.en: The dragon of Rhodes is said to have terrorised the Soudourli valley at the foot of Mount Saint Stephen in the 1340s, under the Knights Hospitaller. It claimed so many victims that Grand Master Hélion de Villeneuve forbade the knights to fight it. Bosio describes it as the size of a horse, with a serpent's head, scaly mule's ears and sharp teeth.

long_description.id: Ksatria Dieudonné de Gozon melanggar larangan itu: ia berlatih dengan naga kayu berengsel, kembali sekitar 1342 bersama dua anjing besar, membunuh naga itu, dan memasang kepalanya di benteng. Legenda serupa sudah ada di Kos sejak 1420, dan sebagian sarjana menduga kisah ini berawal dari hewan nyata.
long_description.en: The knight Dieudonné de Gozon defied the ban: he trained with an articulated wooden dragon, returned around 1342 with two mastiffs, killed the dragon and set its head on the walls. A similar legend existed on Kos from 1420, and some scholars think the story stems from a real animal.

role.en: Terrorised the islanders.

famous_for.en: Killed by Dieudonné de Gozon.

statement.en: The knight Dieudonné de Gozon went home to train with an articulated wooden dragon, then returned to Rhodes around 1342 with two mastiffs, killed the dragon and set its head on the city walls.

short_description.id: Zaldi, "kuda", adalah roh berwujud kuda dalam mitologi Basque, wujud yang diambil penyihir dan Mari, termasuk kuda putih tanpa kepala yang menandakan kematian.
short_description.en: Zaldi, 'horse', is a horse-shaped spirit of Basque mythology, a form taken by witches and by Mari, including the headless white horse that foretells death.

long_description.id: Zaldi, "kuda" dalam bahasa Basque, adalah irelu atau roh dalam legenda Basque. Kuda adalah salah satu wujud yang diambil para penyihir (sorginak) dan juga dewi Mari, dan sejumlah roh bawah tanah digambarkan berwujud kuda. Dari gua Laxarrigibel dekat Tardets keluar makhluk berupa kuda putih yang pernah menyekap seorang pemuda.
long_description.en: Zaldi, Basque for 'horse', is an irelu or spirit of Basque legend. The horse is one of the forms taken by the witches (sorginak) and by the goddess Mari, and some underground spirits appear as horses. From the Laxarrigibel cave near Tardets comes a white-horse being that once held a young man captive.

long_description.id: Zamari zuria, kuda putih tanpa kepala di pegunungan Basque, menandakan kematian; di Soule dan Gipuzkoa ia diperankan penari sebagai roh serealia. Dalam legenda Obantzun, kuda betina hitam membawa seorang pelayan ke jurang dan ia tak kembali. Tokoh Zamaltzain dalam maskarade Zuberoa memakai kostum kuda.
long_description.en: Zamari zuria, a headless white horse of the Basque mountains, foretells death; in Soule and Gipuzkoa a dancer plays it as the cereal spirit. In the Obantzun legend a black mare carries a servant girl into a chasm and she never returns. The Zamaltzain of the Zuberoa masquerades wears a horse costume.

short_description.id: Chudo-Yudo adalah tokoh dongeng rakyat Rusia yang sering bersifat ikan; dalam satu dongeng terkenal ia berupa sekelompok ular berkepala banyak yang membakar kota dan desa.
short_description.en: Chudo-Yudo is a character of Russian folk tales that often has fish-like traits; in one famous tale it is a group of many-headed serpents that burn towns and villages.

long_description.id: Chudo-Yudo, juga disebut "keajaiban laut", adalah tokoh dongeng rakyat Rusia yang sering memiliki ciri dan sifat ikan. Para etnografer dan ahli budaya belum sepakat tentang asal-usul tokoh ini.
long_description.en: Chudo-Yudo, also called the "sea wonder", is a character of Russian folk tales that often has the traits and nature of a fish. Ethnographers and cultural scholars have not agreed on the origin of the figure.

long_description.id: Dalam dongeng "Ivan, Anak Petani, dan Chudo-Yudo", Chudo-Yudo adalah sekelompok ular berkepala enam, sembilan, dan dua belas yang tinggal di seberang Sungai Smorodina dan menyeberang lewat Jembatan Kalinov. Ia digambarkan menunggang kuda dan membakar kota serta desa. Chudo-Yudo berkepala dua belas punya jari berapi yang dapat menumbuhkan kembali kepala yang terpenggal. Ia tinggal di istana batu bersama istri-istri penyihir dan ibu ularnya, dan lawan utamanya adalah Ivan, anak petani.
long_description.en: In the tale "Ivan the Peasant's Son and Chudo-Yudo", Chudo-Yudo is a group of six-, nine- and twelve-headed serpents living beyond the River Smorodina and crossing by the Kalinov Bridge. It is shown riding a horse and burning towns and villages. The twelve-headed Chudo-Yudo has a fiery finger that regrows severed heads. It lives in stone chambers with sorceress wives and a serpent mother, and its chief opponent is Ivan, the peasant's son.

long_description.id: A. N. Afanasyev mencatat bahwa dalam beberapa versi dongeng tentang Raja Laut, peran sang raja diberikan kepada ular, setan, atau Chudo-Yudo yang durjana, dan menurutnya nama Chudo-Yudo kebanyakan diberikan kepada ular mitis, yaitu naga-awan. Max Vasmer menganggap "yudo" kemungkinan besar hanya bentukan berima dari kata "chudo".
long_description.en: A. N. Afanasyev noted that in some versions of the tale of the Sea King the king's role passes to a serpent, the devil or the lawless Chudo-Yudo, and in his view the name Chudo-Yudo is mostly given to the mythical serpent, the dragon-cloud. Max Vasmer thought "yudo" most likely just a rhyming formation modelled on "chudo".

statement.id: Dalam dongeng "Ivan, Anak Petani, dan Chudo-Yudo", Chudo-Yudo adalah sekelompok ular berkepala 6, 9, dan 12 (enam, sembilan, dua belas) yang jahat, tinggal di seberang Sungai Smorodina dan menyeberang lewat Jembatan Kalinov, digambarkan menunggang kuda, dan membakar kota serta desa.
statement.en: In the tale "Ivan the Peasant's Son and Chudo-Yudo", Chudo-Yudo is a group of evil 6-, 9- and 12-headed serpents living beyond the River Smorodina, crossing by the Kalinov Bridge, shown on horseback, burning towns and villages.

short_description.id: Faronika adalah ikan atau ular air dalam cerita rakyat Slovenia yang memikul bumi di punggungnya; geraknya menyebabkan gempa.
short_description.en: Faronika is a fish or water serpent of Slovene folklore that carries the earth on its back; its movements cause earthquakes.

long_description.id: Faronika adalah ikan atau ular air dalam cerita rakyat Slovenia yang memikul bumi di punggungnya. Gerakannya menyebabkan gempa bumi, dan bila ia menyelam, dunia akan berakhir. Ikan atau ular yang terkait samudra kosmis adalah motif umum dalam banyak kosmologi mitis.
long_description.en: Faronika is a fish or water serpent of Slovene folklore that carries the earth on its back. Its movements cause earthquakes, and if it dives the world will end. A fish or serpent linked to the cosmic ocean is a common motif in many mythical cosmologies.

long_description.id: Namanya berasal dari Firaun dalam Alkitab yang tenggelam di Laut Merah, yang menurut kepercayaan rakyat Slovenia berubah menjadi ikan. Orang Slovenia dari Zámuří justru mengenal dua ikan yang berputar di air mengelilingi bumi dan menimbulkan gempa saat menggesek atau memukulnya dengan ekor.
long_description.en: Its name comes from the biblical Pharaoh who drowned in the Red Sea and, according to Slovene folk belief, turned into a fish. Slovenes from Zámuří instead know two fish circling the earth in the waters, causing earthquakes when they rub against it or strike it with their tails.

long_description.id: Kisah Faronika kemudian bercampur dengan legenda Veronika dari Mali Grad dekat Kamnik, yang karena ketamakannya diubah menjadi setengah perempuan setengah ular. Ikan Faronika juga muncul dalam kisah Slavia lama tentang penciptaan dunia yang terkait Kekristenan, saat yang ada hanyalah Tuhan, Matahari, dan laut.
long_description.en: The tale of Faronika later merged with the legend of Veronika of Mali Grad near Kamnik, who was turned into half woman, half snake for her greed. The fish Faronika also appears in an Old Slavic, Christian-linked story of the creation of the world, when only God, the Sun and the sea existed.

short_description.id: Gizotso adalah manusia serigala mitologi Basque, monster setengah manusia setengah serigala yang tinggal di sekitar hutan dan muncul pada malam hari berbalut rantai.
short_description.en: Gizotso is the werewolf of Basque mythology, a half-man, half-wolf monster living near the woods and appearing at night laden with chains.

long_description.id: Gizotso, dari gizon "manusia" dan otso "serigala", adalah manusia serigala Basque: monster setengah manusia setengah serigala yang tinggal di sekitar hutan dan muncul pada malam hari dengan rantai. Di Luzaide ia dipercaya sangat kuat, dan di Agiano dekat Zeanuri ia dianggap lahir dari hubungan binatang dan perempuan; di sana ia konon menyerang seorang perempuan yang bergegas pulang.
long_description.en: Gizotso, from gizon 'man' and otso 'wolf', is the Basque werewolf: a half-man, half-wolf monster living around the woods and appearing at night in chains. At Luzaide it is thought immensely strong, and at Agiano near Zeanuri it is held to be born of a beast and a woman; there it reportedly attacked a woman hurrying home.

long_description.id: Sumber berbeda soal luka perempuan itu: payudaranya dirobek atau matanya dicungkil. Gizotso berbeda dari Otsoko, personifikasi serigala, dan Pierre de Lancre pada 1612 sudah menulis tentang "Monsieur La Forêt" yang meneror Pyrenees.
long_description.en: Sources differ on the woman's wounds: her breasts torn off or her eyes torn out. Gizotso is distinct from Otsoko, the personified wolf, and in 1612 Pierre de Lancre already wrote of a 'Monsieur La Forêt' haunting the Pyrenees.

short_description.id: Hobangoas atau Habergeiß adalah sosok setan dalam kepercayaan rakyat Bayern dan Austria, berwujud kambing berkuku kuda atau burung cacat, yang kini tampil dalam arak-arakan Perchten dan Krampus.
short_description.en: The Hobangoas or Habergeiß is a demonic figure of folk belief in Bavaria and Austria, shaped like a goat with horse's hooves or a deformed bird, who now appears in Perchten and Krampus processions.

long_description.id: Habergeiß (dalam dialek Bayern Habergoaß atau Hobangoas) adalah sosok setan berwujud kambing berkuku kuda, atau burung yang bersuara kambing atau cacat dengan cara lain. Ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk chthonic, setan tumbuhan, atau roh unsur, campuran kambing dan burung, dan dahulu berperan penting dalam kepercayaan rakyat.
long_description.en: The Habergeiß (Bavarian Habergoaß or Hobangoas) is a demonic figure shaped like a goat with horse's hooves, or a bird with a goat's voice or some other deformity. It is described as a chthonic beast, vegetation demon or elemental spirit, a goat-bird hybrid, and once played an important role in folk belief.

long_description.id: Dalam legenda rakyat ia biasanya kambing jantan berkaki tiga dengan mata menyala dan janggut panjang, kadang berbulu burung alih-alih rambut, dan melihatnya dianggap pertanda buruk. Dalam wujud burung ia digambarkan jelek dan berkaki tiga, berbulu merah darah atau kuning menurut daerah, dengan embikan yang menakutkan, dan konon mengisap darah petani dan ternak.
long_description.en: In folk legend it is usually a three-legged billy goat with glowing eyes and a long beard, sometimes feathered instead of furred, and seeing it is a bad omen. In bird form it is ugly and three-legged, blood-red or yellow depending on the region, with a frightening bleat, and is said to suck the blood of farmers and livestock.

long_description.id: Sosok ini masih hidup dalam adat Austria, terutama di Kärnten, Salzburg, dan Steiermark: dalam arak-arakan Krampus pada 5–6 Desember ia mengiringi para Perchten sambil memanggul keranjang "Zistl", dan anak-anak diberi tahu bahwa ia membawa pergi anak nakal di dalamnya. Ia juga muncul dalam karnaval dan adat tiang Mei; menurut legenda lama, ia hewan peliharaan para Perchten dan jauh lebih kuat daripada mereka.
long_description.en: The figure lives on in custom in Austria, especially in Carinthia, Salzburg and Styria: in the Krampus runs of 5–6 December it accompanies the Perchten carrying a 'Zistl' basket, and children are told it carries off naughty children in it. It also appears at carnival and in maypole customs; an old legend makes it the pet of the Perchten, far stronger than they are.

statement.id: Habergeiß (Bayern: Habergoaß) adalah sosok setan berwujud kambing berkuku kuda atau burung yang bersuara kambing atau cacat dengan cara lain.
statement.en: The Habergeiß (Bavarian dialect of Bavaria: Habergoaß) is a demon figure shaped like a goat with horse's hooves or a bird that has a goat's voice or is otherwise deformed.

claims.quote: In der Volkssage wird die Habergeiß meist als dreibeiniger Geißbock mit glühenden Augen und langem Bart beschrieben. In einigen Sagen besitzt dieser Geißbock kein Fell, sondern ein Gefieder. Die Habergeiß zu sehen gilt als böses Omen. Laut einer alten Sage ist die Habergeiß das Haustier der Perchten und übertrifft sie in der Stärke überragend.

statement.id: Dalam legenda rakyat Habergeiß biasanya kambing jantan berkaki tiga bermata menyala dan berjanggut panjang, kadang berbulu burung; melihatnya pertanda buruk; menurut legenda lama ia hewan peliharaan para Perchten dan jauh lebih kuat dari mereka.
statement.en: In folk legend the Habergeiß is mostly a three-legged billy goat with glowing eyes and a long beard, sometimes feathered; seeing it is an evil omen; an old legend makes it the Perchten's pet, far surpassing them in strength.

claims.quote: Bei den Krampusläufen Anfang Dezember (vor allem 5./6. Dezember, Nikolaus) ist die sogenannte Habergeiß unterwegs, die Begleitung der Perchten ist. Sie trägt dabei immer eine „Zistl“ auf dem Rücken, einen Tragekorb, wie er früher bei Bauern üblich war. Den Kindern wird gerne erzählt, die Habergeiß nähme in dieser Zistl die Kinder mit sich fort.

statement.id: Dalam arak-arakan Krampus awal Desember (5–6 Desember, Nikolaus), Habergeiß mengiringi para Perchten sambil memanggul keranjang "Zistl"; anak-anak diberi tahu ia membawa pergi anak-anak di dalamnya; bentuk ini terutama di Kärnten, Salzburg, dan Steiermark (Austria).
statement.en: At the early-December Krampus runs (5–6 December, Nikolaus) the Habergeiß accompanies the Perchten carrying a 'Zistl' basket; children are told it takes children away in it; this form is found mainly in Carinthia (Kärnten), Salzburg and Styria (Steiermark), Austria.

claims.quote: Hierbei wird die Habergeiß als hässlicher, dämonischer Vogel, manchmal mit drei Beinen, beschrieben. Das Fell (manchmal auch Gefieder) ist je nach Gegend rot wie Blut oder gelb. Das Meckern klingt immer erschreckend und furchteinflößend. Es wird ihr nachgesagt, dass sie Bauern und Vieh das Blut aus den Adern saugt.

statement.en: The Habergeiß is also described as an ugly demonic bird, sometimes three-legged, blood-red or yellow by region, with a frightening bleat, said to suck the blood from the veins of farmers and livestock.

statement.id: Hobangoas atau Howangoas, juga Habergoaß, adalah makhluk chthonic, setan tumbuhan, atau roh unsur berwujud kambing yang selalu cacat dengan suatu cara (campuran kambing dan burung).
statement.en: The Hobangoas or Howangoas, also Habergoaß, is a chthonic beast, vegetation demon or elemental spirit in goat form, always deformed in some way (a goat-bird hybrid).

statement.id: Habergeiß berakar kuat dalam adat dan dipakai dalam berbagai adat lokal di sebagian Austria (Österreichs), terutama karnaval, adat tiang Mei, dan arak-arakan Perchten.
statement.en: The Habergeiß is firmly rooted in custom and used in various local customs in parts of Austria (Österreichs), above all carnival, maypole customs and Perchten runs.

claims.quote: Das Kompositionsglied Haber bezeichnet ‚Ziegenbock‘ (vgl. mundartlich Häberling ‚einjähriger Ziegenbock‘), Geiß ‚Ziege, Zicke‘. Dieser Name sowie gleichbedeutende Bockgeiß sind tautologische Komposita, und die oft gehörte Darstellung, nach der gleichlautende Haber ‚Hafer‘ bedeute, lässt sich etymologisch nicht halten.

statement.id: Unsur Haber berarti "kambing jantan" dan Geiß "kambing betina"; nama ini kata majemuk tautologis, dan anggapan umum bahwa Haber berarti "haver/oat" (Hafer) tidak dapat dipertahankan secara etimologis; dalam bahasa Islandia Kuno hafr berarti kambing jantan.
statement.en: The element Haber means 'billy goat' and Geiß 'goat'; the name is a tautological compound, and the common view that Haber means 'oat' (Hafer) cannot be upheld etymologically; in Old Icelandic hafr means buck.

claims.quote: Mythologisch findet sie in Skandinavien ihre Entsprechung im Julbock, in Rumänien in der Capra.

statement.en: Mythologically its counterpart in Scandinavia is the Julbock, and in Romania the Capra.

short_description.id: Kuperan adalah raksasa (Riese) dalam lingkaran kisah Siegfried pembunuh naga, pemegang kunci gunung tempat seekor naga tinggal.
short_description.en: Kuperan is a giant (Riese) in the cycle of tales about Siegfried the dragon-slayer, keeper of the key to a mountain where a dragon lives.

long_description.id: Kuperan adalah raksasa (Riese) dalam lingkaran kisah Siegfried pembunuh naga (Drachentöter), yang memegang kunci masuk ke sebuah gunung tempat naga bersarang. Dalam puisi tentang Seyfrid, Siegfried berusaha membebaskan putri Kriemhild yang ditawan naga, dibantu kurcaci Eugel serta raksasa Kuperan yang enggan dan berkhianat.
long_description.en: Kuperan is a giant (Riese) in the cycle of tales about Siegfried the dragon-slayer (Drachentöter), holding the key that opens a mountain where a dragon lairs. In the poem about Seyfrid, Siegfried sets out to free the princess Kriemhild held by the dragon, helped by the dwarf Eugel and by the unwilling, treacherous giant Kuperan.

long_description.id: Eugel memberi tahu Siegfried bahwa raksasa Kuperan tinggal di dekat situ dan memegang kunci gunung. Mereka bertarung, dan Siegfried mengampuni raksasa yang terluka itu dengan syarat ia membantu membebaskan Kriemhild. Namun di hutan Kuperan menyerang Siegfried hingga pingsan, dan Eugel menutupi sang pahlawan dengan jubah tak kasatmata. Kuperan kemudian menunjukkan pedang yang mampu mengalahkan naga, tetapi menyerang lagi; kali ini Siegfried mendorongnya dari batu karang hingga hancur berkeping-keping. Artikel de menyebut Kuperan berkhianat dua kali, sedangkan ringkasan en menyebut serangan ketiga.
long_description.en: Eugel tells Siegfried that the giant Kuperan lives nearby and holds the key to the mountain. They fight, and Siegfried spares the wounded giant on condition that he help free Kriemhild. But in the forest Kuperan strikes Siegfried senseless, and Eugel covers the hero with his cloak of invisibility. Kuperan later reveals a sword able to defeat the dragon, yet attacks again; this time Siegfried pushes him off the rock and he shatters into pieces. The de article says Kuperan betrayed him twice, while the en summary speaks of a third attack.

text.id: Namanya tercatat sejak 1589; wujud mirip kuda baru muncul dalam catatan abad kedelapan belas.
text.en: Its name is recorded from 1589; the horse-like form appears only in 18th-century records.

short_description.id: Tikbalang adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Filipina yang berkeliaran di pegunungan dan hutan, digambarkan tinggi kurus dengan kepala dan kuku kuda, dan terkenal karena menyesatkan para pejalan.
short_description.en: The tikbalang is a creature of Philippine folklore that haunts mountains and forests, pictured as tall and bony with a horse's head and hooves, and known for leading travellers astray.

long_description.id: Tikbalang adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Filipina yang konon mengintai di pegunungan dan hutan hujan. Ia digambarkan sebagai sosok mirip manusia yang tinggi dan kurus, berkepala dan berkuku kuda, dengan tungkai sangat panjang hingga lututnya melewati kepala saat berjongkok. Dalam beberapa versi, ia adalah jelmaan janin yang digugurkan dan dikirim ke bumi dari limbo.
long_description.en: The tikbalang belongs to the folklore of the Philippines, where it is said to haunt mountains and rainforests. It is pictured as a tall, bony humanlike figure with a horse's head and hooves and limbs so long that its knees rise above its head when it squats. In some versions it is an aborted fetus transformed and sent to earth from limbo.

long_description.id: Catatan tertulis awal tidak menyebut wujud kuda, karena kuda bukan hewan asli Filipina sebelum masa Spanyol. Juan de Plasencia (1589) hanya menyebut tigbalaang sebagai hantu atau penampakan. Pada abad kedelapan belas, Juan Francisco de San Antonio menggambarkannya sebagai makhluk jahat di pegunungan yang dapat berubah menjadi orang tua, kuda, atau monster, dan Juan José Delgado sekitar 1750 menjadi yang pertama menggambarkannya sebagai manusia-kuda.
long_description.en: Early written records do not mention a horse form, as horses were not native to the Philippines before the Spanish era. Juan de Plasencia (1589) names the tigbalaang only as a phantom. In the 18th century, Juan Francisco de San Antonio described it as a malevolent mountain being able to appear as an old man, a horse or a monster, and Juan José Delgado around 1750 was the first to describe it as a werehorse.

long_description.id: Tikbalang dikaitkan dengan tempat gelap, sepi, dan rimbun: di bawah jembatan, rumpun bambu, kebun pisang, atau di atas pohon kalumpang dan balete. Sebagian orang Filipina percaya tikbalang menghuni pohon sebagai penjaganya. Ia menakuti pejalan, menyesatkan mereka, dan membuat mereka kembali ke jalan yang sama sejauh apa pun mereka pergi; memakai baju terbalik atau meminta izin dengan suara keras dipercaya dapat menangkalnya.
long_description.en: The tikbalang is linked with dark, lonely, overgrown places: under bridges, in bamboo clumps or banana groves, and atop kalumpang or balete trees. Some Filipinos believe tikbalangs inhabit trees as their guardians. It frightens travellers, leads them astray and makes them return to the same path however far they go; wearing one's shirt inside out or asking permission aloud is believed to counter this.

long_description.id: Peneliti Jordan Clark menekankan bahwa sejarah nama tikbalang perlu dipisahkan dari sejarah citranya. Menurut penelusurannya, catatan kolonial menunjukkan perkembangan dari makhluk hutan bernama tanpa gambaran fisik pada 1589, lalu penampakan gunung bersayap dan berbau pada 1613, makhluk yang dapat berganti wujud sekitar 1731, hingga raksasa berkaki kuda pada 1763.
long_description.en: Researcher Jordan Clark stresses that the history of the tikbalang's name should be separated from the history of its image. His survey of colonial records traces a sequence: a named wilderness being with no physical description in 1589, a mountain apparition with wings and a smell in 1613, a shape-changing being around 1731, and a giant with horse legs in 1763.

cultural_context.id: Di kalangan orang Tagalog awal, ungkapan 'Tigbalang ca mandin!' dipakai untuk mencela orang yang berperilaku tidak pantas atau tidak beradab.
cultural_context.en: Among the early Tagalogs, the expression 'Tigbalang ca mandin!' was used to rebuke someone whose behaviour was improper or uncivilized.

claims.quote: is a creature of Philippine folklore said to lurk in the mountains and rainforests of the Philippines. It is a tall, bony humanoid creature with the head and hooves of a horse and disproportionately long limbs, to the point that its knees reach above its head when it squats down. In some versions, it is a transformation of an aborted fetus sent to earth from limbo.

statement.id: Tikbalang (juga Tigbalang, Tigbalan, Tikbalan, Tigbolan) adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Filipina yang mengintai di pegunungan dan hutan hujan; tinggi, kurus, berkepala dan berkuku kuda, bertungkai sangat panjang hingga lututnya melewati kepala saat berjongkok; dalam beberapa versi ia jelmaan janin yang digugurkan dan dikirim dari limbo.
statement.en: The tikbalang (also Tigbalang, Tigbalan, Tikbalan, Tigbolan) is a Philippine folklore creature lurking in mountains and rainforests; tall, bony, with a horse's head and hooves and limbs so long its knees pass its head when squatting; in some versions it is an aborted fetus sent from limbo.

claims.quote: As horses weren't native to the Philippines in the pre-Spanish era, the earliest written records about the tikbalang did not specify horse or animal morphology.

statement.id: Karena kuda bukan hewan asli Filipina sebelum masa Spanyol, catatan tertulis awal tentang tikbalang tidak menyebut wujud kuda.
statement.en: As horses were not native to the pre-Spanish Philippines, the earliest records of the tikbalang do not specify a horse form.

claims.quote: There were also ghosts, which they called vibit; and phantoms, which they called Tigbalaang.

statement.id: Plasencia menulis bahwa ada hantu yang disebut vibit dan penampakan yang disebut Tigbalaang.
statement.en: Plasencia wrote that there were ghosts called vibit and phantoms called Tigbalaang.

claims.quote: Among the early Tagalogs, the derogatory expression “Tigbalang ca mandin!”, literally translated as “You are a wild beast!”, was used to describe a person whose behavior was considered improper or socially unacceptable.

statement.id: Di kalangan orang Tagalog awal, ungkapan hinaan 'Tigbalang ca mandin!' ('Kau binatang liar!') dipakai untuk orang yang berperilaku tidak pantas.
statement.en: Among early Tagalogs, the insult 'Tigbalang ca mandin!' ('You are a wild beast!') described someone whose behaviour was improper.

claims.quote: Juan Francisco de San Antonio's Cronicas(1738-1744) describes the tikbalang as a malevolent entity living in the mountains, able to shapeshift into a variety of forms, including horses.

statement.id: Cronicas (1738-1744) karya Juan Francisco de San Antonio menggambarkan tikbalang sebagai makhluk jahat di pegunungan yang dapat berubah menjadi berbagai wujud, termasuk kuda.
statement.en: Juan Francisco de San Antonio's Cronicas (1738-1744) describes the tikbalang as a malevolent mountain being able to take many forms, including horses.

claims.quote: it has been wont to appear to them in the mountains—now in the guise of an old man, telling them that he is their nono; now as a horse; and now as a monster.

statement.id: Menurut Cronicas, tikbalang biasa menampakkan diri di pegunungan sebagai orang tua yang mengaku leluhur mereka, sebagai kuda, atau sebagai monster.
statement.en: According to the Cronicas, it appeared in the mountains as an old man claiming to be their ancestor, as a horse, or as a monster.

claims.quote: However, the very first document to actually describe the tikbalang as specifically having the appearance of a werehorse as it is more commonly known is Juan José Delgado's Biblioteca Histórica Filipina (orig. c. 1750).

statement.id: Dokumen pertama yang menggambarkan tikbalang sebagai manusia-kuda adalah Biblioteca Histórica Filipina karya Juan José Delgado (sekitar 1750).
statement.en: The first document describing the tikbalang as a werehorse is Juan José Delgado's Biblioteca Histórica Filipina (c. 1750).

claims.quote: Delgado also mentions the name "unglo" being used by the Visayans to refer to the same creature as the tikbalang.

statement.id: Delgado menyebut orang Visayas memakai nama unglo untuk makhluk yang sama.
statement.en: Delgado notes the Visayans used the name unglo for the same creature.

claims.quote: Tikbalang is generally associated with dark, sparsely populated, foliage-overgrown areas, with legends variously identifying their habitat as being beneath bridges, in bamboo clumps or banana groves, and atop Kalumpang (Sterculia foetida) or Balite (Ficus indica) trees.

statement.id: Tikbalang dikaitkan dengan tempat gelap, sepi, dan rimbun, seperti di bawah jembatan, rumpun bambu, kebun pisang, atau di atas pohon kalumpang dan balete.
statement.en: The tikbalang is linked with dark, lonely, overgrown places such as under bridges, bamboo clumps, banana groves, or atop kalumpang and balete trees.

claims.quote: Tikbalangs or Tigbolan scare travelers, lead them astray and play tricks on them such as making them return to an arbitrary path no matter how far they go or turn. Wearing one’s shirt inside out is believed to counteract this. Another countermeasure is to ask permission aloud to pass by

statement.id: Tikbalang menakuti dan menyesatkan pejalan, membuat mereka kembali ke jalan yang sama; memakai baju terbalik atau meminta izin lewat dengan keras dipercaya menangkalnya.
statement.en: Tikbalangs scare and mislead travellers, making them return to the same path; wearing a shirt inside out or asking permission aloud is believed to counter this.

claims.quote: Taken together, the four records show an identifiable progression: the named but physically undescribed Tigbalaang in 1589; a winged and odorous mountain apparition in 1613; a being able to assume several forms by about 1731; and a giant with horse legs in 1763.

statement.id: Empat catatan kolonial menunjukkan perkembangan: Tigbalaang tanpa gambaran fisik (1589), penampakan gunung bersayap dan berbau (1613), makhluk yang dapat berganti wujud (sekitar 1731), dan raksasa berkaki kuda (1763).
statement.en: Four colonial records show a progression: an undescribed Tigbalaang (1589), a winged, odorous mountain apparition (1613), a multi-form being (c. 1731), and a giant with horse legs (1763).

claims.quote: Individual tikbalangs, even today among superstitious Filipinos, are thought to inhabit trees as guardians

statement.id: Sebagian orang Filipina hingga kini percaya tikbalang menghuni pohon sebagai penjaganya.
statement.en: Some Filipinos still believe tikbalangs inhabit trees as guardians.

claims.quote: This article separates the history of the name from the history of the image.

statement.id: Jordan Clark memisahkan sejarah nama tikbalang dari sejarah citranya.
statement.en: Jordan Clark separates the history of the tikbalang's name from the history of its image.

claims.quote: San Buenaventura records a belief that the tigbalang had wings and carried people where it wished. Those taken away were said to grow weak and die.

statement.id: San Buenaventura mencatat kepercayaan bahwa tigbalang bersayap dan membawa orang ke mana ia mau; yang dibawa menjadi lemah lalu meninggal.
statement.en: San Buenaventura records a belief that the tigbalang had wings and carried people where it wished; those taken grew weak and died.

claims.quote: (also Tigbalang, Tigbalan, Tikbalan, Tigbolan, or Werehorse) is a creature of Philippine folklore

statement.id: Tikbalang juga disebut Tigbalang, Tigbalan, Tikbalan, Tigbolan, atau manusia-kuda.
statement.en: The tikbalang is also called Tigbalang, Tigbalan, Tikbalan, Tigbolan or werehorse.

summary.en: Early records (1589) give no form; 1613 describes it as winged.

short_description.id: Vellamo adalah dewi air, danau, dan laut dalam mitologi Finlandia, istri dewa laut Ahti, yang dihormati para nelayan.
short_description.en: Vellamo is the goddess of water, lakes and seas in Finnish mythology, wife of the sea god Ahti and revered by fishermen.

long_description.id: Vellamo, juga dieja Wellamo, adalah dewi air, danau, dan laut dalam mitologi Finlandia yang dijuluki Veen emäntä, "Nyonya Air". Suaminya ialah dewa laut Ahti, dan dalam mantra memancing Finlandia keduanya diminta menggiring ternak mereka, yaitu ikan, ke dalam jaring.
long_description.en: Vellamo, whose name is also written Wellamo, is the Finnish mythological goddess of seas, lakes and water in general, called Veen emäntä, 'Mistress of Water'. Her husband is the sea god Ahti, and Finnish fishing spells ask the two of them to drive their cattle, meaning fish, into the nets.

long_description.id: Dalam lagu-lagu runik, Nyonya Air memiliki sapi-sapi yang kadang diberikannya kepada orang miskin; saat sapi-sapinya merumput di pantai, ia duduk agak jauh di atas batu sambil menyisir rambut. Ia dihormati khususnya oleh para nelayan, karena melihatnya walau dari jauh menjamin tangkapan melimpah. Ia juga digambarkan tinggal bersama Ahti di istana bawah laut Ahtola dan menggiring sapi ajaibnya ke permukaan saat kabut pagi untuk memakan buih laut.
long_description.en: In runic songs the Mistress of Water owns cows that she sometimes gives to poor people; while they graze on the beach she sits a little way off on a rock combing her hair. Fishermen especially revered her, since seeing her even from afar guaranteed a rich catch. She is also described as living with Ahti in the undersea palace of Ahtola and leading her magic cows to the surface in the morning mist to eat sea foam.

long_description.id: Nama Vellamo diduga berasal dari kata Finlandia velloa, "mengaduk", yang menggambarkan gerak air dan ombak; Kaarle Krohn dan Uno Harva menganggapnya nama yang terbentuk belakangan. Ia digambarkan tinggi dan cantik, bergaun biru dari lumut laut, kadang berekor ikan seperti putri duyung, sebagaimana pada lambang Päijät-Häme. Sebuah lagu runik Karelia Selatan menyebut Näkki sebagai keturunan Vellamo dan Ahti.
long_description.en: The name Vellamo is thought to come from Finnish velloa, 'to churn', which evokes moving water and waves; Kaarle Krohn and Uno Harva considered it a later-formed name. She is described as tall and beautiful in a blue dress of sea moss, sometimes with a fish tail like a mermaid, as on the arms of Päijät-Häme. A South Karelian runic song calls the Näkki the offspring of Vellamo and Ahti.

short_description.id: Bäckahästen, "kuda sungai", adalah kuda air dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, terutama Skåne: kuda putih megah yang memikat orang, terutama anak-anak, menungganginya lalu menenggelamkan mereka.
short_description.en: Bäckahästen, the 'brook horse', is a water horse of Scandinavian, especially Scanian, folklore: a majestic white horse that lures people, above all children, onto its back and drowns them.

long_description.id: Bäckahästen (dari bahasa Swedia bäck, "sungai kecil", dan hästen, "kuda") dalam kepercayaan rakyat Skåne adalah roh sungai atau Näck dalam wujud kuda. Ia dapat dibandingkan dengan kuda air mitologi Kelt seperti each uisge dari Skotlandia, kelpie, dan ceffyl dŵr dari Wales.
long_description.en: Bäckahästen (from Swedish bäck, 'brook', and hästen, 'the horse') is, in Scanian folk belief, the spirit of a brook or the Näck in horse form. It can be compared with the water horses of Celtic mythology such as the Scottish each uisge, the kelpie and the Welsh ceffyl dŵr.

long_description.id: Ia pemangsa licik yang mengintai di sungai dan danau untuk menyeret penunggang dan kuda lain ke air. Wujudnya kuda jantan gagah yang biasanya putih berkilau, kadang kelabu, hitam, atau kebiruan, dengan mulut penuh taring tajam, dan sering muncul saat berkabut. Siapa yang naik ke punggungnya tak bisa turun lagi, dan punggungnya makin panjang semakin banyak anak yang naik.
long_description.en: It is a treacherous predator lurking in brooks, rivers and lakes to drag riders and other horses into the water. It appears as a fine stallion, usually shining white, sometimes dapple-grey, black or bluish, with a mouth full of sharp fangs, and often shows itself in fog. Whoever climbs onto its back cannot get down, and its back grows longer the more children climb on.

long_description.id: Untuk mencegahnya menenggelamkan anak-anak, orang dapat melempar sepotong baja di antara kuda itu dan air, sehingga kekuatannya patah; anak yang menyerukan kata "salib" juga membuatnya melempar mereka dan menghilang. Kuda ini juga bisa dipasangi bajak dan bekerja keras sepanjang hari, karena dijinakkan oleh baja pada tali kekangnya.
long_description.en: To stop it drowning children one can throw a piece of steel between the horse and the water, breaking its power; a child calling out the word 'cross' also makes it throw them off and vanish. It can also be put to the plough and work hard all day, tamed by the steel in its harness.

who.en: A drowning water horse.

role.id: Memikat orang naik lalu menceburkan mereka ke air.
role.en: Lures riders on and plunges them into water.

famous_for.id: Punggung yang memanjang untuk banyak anak.
famous_for.en: A back that lengthens for many children.

did_you_know.id: Menurut kepercayaan Swedia, punggung bäckahäst makin panjang semakin banyak anak yang menaikinya.
did_you_know.en: In Swedish belief the bäckahäst's back grows longer the more children climb onto it.

description.id: Sepotong baja yang dilempar di antara kuda dan air mematahkan kekuatannya.

short_description.id: Bäckahästen, "kuda sungai", adalah kuda air dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, terutama Skåne: kuda putih megah yang memikat orang, terutama anak-anak, menungganginya lalu menenggelamkan mereka.
short_description.en: Bäckahästen, the 'brook horse', is a water horse of Scandinavian, especially Scanian, folklore: a majestic white horse that lures people, above all children, onto its back and drowns them.

long_description.id: Bäckahästen (dari bahasa Swedia bäck, "sungai kecil", dan hästen, "kuda") dalam kepercayaan rakyat Skåne adalah roh sungai atau Näck dalam wujud kuda. Ia dapat dibandingkan dengan kuda air mitologi Kelt seperti each uisge dari Skotlandia, kelpie, dan ceffyl dŵr dari Wales.
long_description.en: Bäckahästen (from Swedish bäck, 'brook', and hästen, 'the horse') is, in Scanian folk belief, the spirit of a brook or the Näck in horse form. It can be compared with the water horses of Celtic mythology such as the Scottish each uisge, the kelpie and the Welsh ceffyl dŵr.

long_description.id: Ia pemangsa licik yang mengintai di sungai dan danau untuk menyeret penunggang dan kuda lain ke air. Wujudnya kuda jantan gagah yang biasanya putih berkilau, kadang kelabu, hitam, atau kebiruan, dengan mulut penuh taring tajam, dan sering muncul saat berkabut. Siapa yang naik ke punggungnya tak bisa turun lagi, dan punggungnya makin panjang semakin banyak anak yang naik.
long_description.en: It is a treacherous predator lurking in brooks, rivers and lakes to drag riders and other horses into the water. It appears as a fine stallion, usually shining white, sometimes dapple-grey, black or bluish, with a mouth full of sharp fangs, and often shows itself in fog. Whoever climbs onto its back cannot get down, and its back grows longer the more children climb on.

long_description.id: Untuk mencegahnya menenggelamkan anak-anak, orang dapat melempar sepotong baja di antara kuda itu dan air, sehingga kekuatannya patah; anak yang menyerukan kata "salib" juga membuatnya melempar mereka dan menghilang. Kuda ini juga bisa dipasangi bajak dan bekerja keras sepanjang hari, karena dijinakkan oleh baja pada tali kekangnya.
long_description.en: To stop it drowning children one can throw a piece of steel between the horse and the water, breaking its power; a child calling out the word 'cross' also makes it throw them off and vanish. It can also be put to the plough and work hard all day, tamed by the steel in its harness.

short_description.id: Basandere, "nyonya hutan", adalah perempuan liar berbulu dalam mitologi Basque, istri Basajaun, yang menyisir rambutnya dengan sisir emas di mulut gua sambil menjaga harta.
short_description.en: Basandere, 'lady of the forest', is a hairy wild woman of Basque mythology, wife of Basajaun, who combs her hair with a golden comb at cave mouths while guarding treasure.

long_description.id: Basandere, "nyonya hutan" atau "nyonya liar", adalah istri Basajaun dalam mitologi Basque, perempuan liar berbulu dan berambut sangat panjang yang tinggal di Pyrenees Basque, terutama hutan Iraty. Ia biasa berada dekat mulut gua atau mata air, menyisir rambut dengan sisir emas sambil mengawasi hartanya, misalnya di gua puncak Gunung Mondarrain; ia lenyap bila didekati.
long_description.en: Basandere, 'lady of the forest' or 'wild lady', is Basajaun's wife in Basque mythology, a hairy wild woman with very long hair living in the Basque Pyrenees, especially the forest of Iraty. She sits by cave mouths or springs combing her hair with a golden comb and watching her treasure, as at the cave on top of Mount Mondarrain; she vanishes when approached.

long_description.id: Kisah gembala yang mencuri sisir emasnya sering diceritakan. Ia mirip "perempuan liar" pelindung alam dan mengingatkan pada Mari dan Encantada.
long_description.en: Tales of a shepherd stealing her golden comb are common. She resembles the nature-protecting 'wild women' and recalls Mari and the Encantada.
